evidence: Cic. Att. 4.2.7: amīcōrum benignitās exhausta est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally to draw out a liquid, to bail (sentīnam exhaurīre, Cic. Sen. 17), to drink up; then to empty a treasury, a province, a people of its money, and to use up anything: patience, kindness, a subject. It also means to undergo, to see through (labōrēs exhaurīre, Liv.).

evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 6: patrimōnium per luxuriam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To use up, spend, eat up (see eat-up): money, time, supplies.

phrases.english: Cheers, but don’t drink it all.
phrases.source: Schottennius, Confabulātiōnēs, Dē pōtū postrēmō ā cēnā

phrases.english: others should bail out the bilge

sources: Lewis & Short: exhaurio · Lewis & Short: consumo

Cicero (Sen. 17) and Schottennius from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-schottenius); Schottennius is sixteenth-century school Latin. The other passages as Lewis & Short quotes them.
